page.layout: One column of running text. Margin notes run down the left margin, damaged and partly illegible. A thin decorative pointer mark sits in the right margin, not text. No printed text below the column apart from faint margin remnants at the foot.

main_text.p: riis, & ferè maximis. Actor in hoc foro δικῶν[?], actio δίκης[?] vocabatur. Iudices pro re natâ ex omnibus civibus sorte ducebantur, qui infra ætatis annum xxx non essent, & essent vitæ integræ, ac ærario non deberent: hi enim hoc judicatu arcebantur. Sortitioni verò huic præerant ix archontes summi in tota republicâ magistratus, cum scribâ.

Sed priusquam ad actionem ipsam veniretur, hæc præcedebant. Primum actor magistratum adibat, cui ista cognitio erat demandata, (hi ut plurimum sex-viri Thesmothetæ erant ex [illegible, ~3 letters]numero ix archontum) ac permissu reum in jus vocabat per [illegible, ~7 letters] [illegible, ~4 letters]atorem, quod [illegible, ~9 letters] dicent. Deinde conceptis verbis actionem ei intentabat, eamq; intentionem tabella descriptam magistratus Iftius [illegible, ~5 letters] aut scribæ tradebat. Cujus formula fuerit, licet ex actione [illegible, ~3 letters]crati intentata apud Diogenem Laërtium, & ex altera intentata Alcibiadi apud Plutarchum in utriusque accusati[?] ita cognoscere. Vsitatum verò erat, formula nomen actoris, rei, citatoris exprimi, & crimen ipsum verbis [illegible, ~3 letters]ucissimis adscribi cum pœna, quæ postulabatur. Tum intra certum tempus
[illegible, ~6 letters] (faint marginal annotation at the foot of the page, largely lost)

page.notes: Left margin: a column of small, faint marginal notes, several of them lost to damage or to show-through from the facing page. Recognisable fragments only: Roman numeral sequences (IIOIIIO), a sign resembling "&" and the mark "1cɔI"; none is legible as a full word. Greek words in the text are doubtful: δικῶν, δίκης, the Greek word beside "per", and ἀρίδῳ/ἀπίδῳ after "Iftius" are read with [?] or marked illegible. "accusati[?]" and the last word of the Latin line are partly covered by margin marks. The word before "ucissimis" (probably "brevissimis") is damaged and not read. The line "pus" continues "tempus" after the hyphen; it is printed on its own line. The right margin shows only a pointer mark and some stains.
